es: Reconocer redundancias, nominalizaciones vacías y relleno en frases recargadas y elegir la versión más directa.

vocabulary.es: redundante, que repite lo ya dicho

teaching.en: This sentence is wordy: it needs twelve words to say what four words can say.

teaching.explanationEs: Wordy = usa más palabras de las necesarias sin añadir información.
segments: This sentence is wordy: it needs twelve words

teaching.en: The phrase "end result" is redundant, because a result always comes at the end.

segments: The phrase "end result" is redundant, because
a result always comes at the end.
teaching.audioText: The phrase "end result" is redundant, because a result always comes at the end.

teaching.en: A concise email keeps the point and cuts the padding.

teaching.explanationEs: Padding = palabras que llenan espacio sin aportar datos.
segments: A concise email keeps the
point and cuts the padding.
teaching.audioText: A concise email keeps the point and cuts the padding.

teaching.en: Instead of "give consideration to", use the direct verb consider.

segments: Instead of "give consideration to",
use the direct verb consider.
teaching.audioText: Instead of "give consideration to", use the direct verb consider.

teaching.en: Do not repeat the same idea: "completely finished" is just "finished".

segments: Do not repeat the same idea:
"completely finished" is just "finished".
teaching.audioText: Do not repeat the same idea: "completely finished" is just "finished".

teaching.en: A plain word is often stronger than a long phrase.

segments: A plain word is often
stronger than a long phrase.
teaching.audioText: A plain word is often stronger than a long phrase.

teaching.en: A warm voice uses friendly words and speaks directly to the reader.

teaching.en: First, edit your draft: cut every word that adds nothing.

teaching.audioText: First, edit your draft: cut every word that adds nothing.

teaching.en: Every change should make the text shorter or clearer.

prompt.es: Edita el borrador: tres cambios de concisión, uno de ritmo y una nota por cambio.

answer.text:
Our school garden club meets every Saturday. Because the yard was empty, the club decided to plant a garden. Every member planted it. We planted beans, flowers and trees. Now the garden is finished. I think it is the best club in the school.
Change 1: I changed "due to the fact that" to "because" because it is shorter and keeps the meaning.
Change 2: I changed "made a decision" to "decided" because the verb is more direct.
Change 3: I changed "each and every member" to "every member" because the words repeated the same idea.
